summary: Multiple cryptographic issues in Python oic
instruction: The package `oic` has a security vulnerability (CWE-325, CWE-347). A regression test describing the required secure behaviour has been added to the repository. Modify the package source so the test passes while keeping existing behaviour intact. Do not edit tests.

advisory.summary: Multiple cryptographic issues in Python oic
advisory.details:
### Impact
* Client implementations using this library

### Issues
1) The IdToken signature algorithm was not checked automatically, but only if the expected algorithm was passed in as a kwarg.
2) JWA `none` algorithm was allowed in all flows.
3) `oic.consumer.Consumer.parse_authz` returns an unverified IdToken. The verification of the token was left to the discretion of the implementator.
4) `iat` claim was not checked for sanity (i.e. it could be in the future)

### Patches
1) IdToken signature is now always checked.
2) JWA `none` algorithm is now allowed only if using the `response_type` `code`
3) IdToken verification is now done automatically.
4) `iat` claim is now checked for sanity.

related_advisories.details: Python oic is a Python OpenID Connect implementation. In Python oic before version 1.2.1, there are several related cryptographic issues affecting client implementations that use the library. The issues are: 1) The IdToken signature algorithm was not checked automatically, but only if the expected algorithm was passed in as a kwarg. 2) JWA `none` algorithm was allowed in all flows. 3) oic.consumer.Consumer.parse_authz returns an unverified IdToken. The verification of the token was left to the discretion of the implementator. 4) iat claim was not checked for sanity (i.e. it could be in the future). These issues are patched in version 1.2.1.
